question: Under whose administration was the practice of Sati officially abolished in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord William Bentinck**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord William Bentinck was the Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.
 
• The practice of Sati, where widows were forced to self-immolate on their husband’s funeral pyre, was officially abolished during his administration in **1829**.
 
• The abolition was enforced through the Bengal Sati Regulation, **Regulation XVII of 1829**, which declared Sati as illegal and punishable by law.
 
• Bentinck took this reform initiative due to advocacy by social reformers like **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, who strongly opposed the practice.
 
• The regulation applied initially to Bengal Presidency and was later extended to other parts of British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:**

 
 
• A prominent social reformer who played a key role in advocating for the abolition of Sati.
 
• He argued that Sati had no religious sanction and was opposed to the core teachings of Hindu scriptures.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of Modern India" for his reformist efforts.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829:**
 
 
• It was enacted on December 4, 1829, by Lord William Bentinck.
 
• The regulation declared the practice of Sati as illegal, punishable by the courts, and equivalent to culpable homicide.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Sati Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition marked a significant step in social reform during British rule in India.
 
• It helped pave the way for future reforms concerning women’s rights and welfare.
 
 
 
• **Lord William Bentinck's Legacy:**
 
 
• Besides abolishing Sati, Bentinck introduced other reforms such as the promotion of Western education and suppression of Thuggee.
 
• He is remembered for his progressive approach toward governance and reform in India.
